(Edmond, Oklahoma) | college = *[[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]] (2021–2024) *[[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]] (2024–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | career_start = 2025 | years1 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team1 = [[Rip City Remix]] | years2 = {{nbay|2025|end}} | team2 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | years3 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]] | team3 = →[[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]] | years4 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team4 = [[Houston Rockets]] | years5 = [[2026–27 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team5 = →[[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] | highlights = * [[NBA G League Rookie of the Year Award|NBA G League Rookie of the Year]] (2026) * Third-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2024) * Third-team [[List of All-SEC men's basketball teams|All-SEC]] (2025) }} '''Sean Pedulla''' (born October 10, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech Hokies]] and the [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss Rebels]]. ==High school career== Pedulla attended [[Edmond Memorial High School]] in [[Edmond, Oklahoma]]. During his junior year, he averaged 17.2 points per game while leading Edmond Memorial to the 2020 state championship, which was cancelled by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. This performance led him to be named to ''[[The Oklahoman]]'s'' Super 5 third-team. In July 2020, Pedulla posted 31 points during an Oklahoma [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU game]], which captured the attention of numerous Division I programs. In the week following the game, Pedulla received offers from [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]], [[Samford Bulldogs men's basketball|Samford]], [[Saint Louis Billikens men's basketball|Saint Louis]], [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa]], and [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]]. A few days prior to the game, he received an offer from [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs basketball|Louisiana Tech]].{{cite news |last1=Jourdan |first1=Cameron |title=Oklahoma high school boys basketball: Edmond Memorial’s Sean Pedulla sees recruitment ramping up |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/07/13/oklahoma-high-school-boys-basketball-edmond-memorials-sean-pedulla-sees-recruitment-ramping-up/60391374007/ |access-date=March 7, 2025 |work=The Oklahoman |date=July 13, 2020}} Ranked as the nation's 141st-best prospect and the 25th-best [[point guard]] in the 2021 class per [[247Sports]], he committed to play college basketball at [[Virginia Tech]] on October 19, 2020, over offers from Minnesota and [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]].{{Cite web |last=Arvin |first=Chris |date=October 19, 2020 |title=Virginia Tech adds talented guard Sean Pedulla |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Virginia-Tech-Basketball-recruiting-commitment-Sean-Pedulla-153226328/ |access-date=December 22, 2022 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}} In his senior year, he again led Edmond Memorial to the championship game and earned a first-team Super 5 selection from ''The Oklahoman''.{{cite news |last1=Jourdan |first1=Cameron |title=Super 5 boys basketball: Meet The Oklahoman's 2021 first-team selections |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2021/04/28/meet-oklahomans-2021-super-5-boys-basketball-first-team/7387688002/ |access-date=March 7, 2025 |work=The Oklahoman |date=April 28, 2021}} ==College career== ===Virginia Tech=== In his freshman year, Pedulla did not start a single one of Virginia Tech's 36 games and averaged 5.4 points.{{Cite web |last=Berman |first=Mark |date=November 29, 2022 |title='Aggressive' Pedulla delivers again in win over Minnesota |url=https://roanoke.com/sports/college/va_tech/aggressive-pedulla-delivers-again-in-win-over-minnesota/article_748284a8-6f9b-11ed-8a5a-8f07dc5f6415.html |access-date=December 22, 2022 |website=The Roanoke Times |language=en}} However, he managed to shoot 45% from beyond the three-point arc, and scored a then-career high 19 points off the bench in the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022 NCAA tournament]] against [[2021–22 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas]].{{Cite web |last=Unruh|first=Jacob|title=How Edmond Memorial alum Sean Pedulla proved doubters wrong with Virginia Tech basketball |date=December 10, 2022|url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/college/cowboys/2022/12/10/virginia-tech-basketball-sean-pedulla-gets-shot-at-oklahoma-state/69716669007/ |access-date=December 22, 2022 |website=The Oklahoman |language=en-US}} Pedulla became the starting point guard for the team during his sophomore season and quickly became a leading contributor. Early on, he emerged as one of the top ACC point guards, and led the team in scoring and assists through their hot 11–1 run.{{Cite web |last=Trotter |first=Isaac |date=December 21, 2022 |title=Circling college basketball’s best breakout performers |url=https://247sports.com/LongFormArticle/Circling-college-basketballs-best-breakout-performers-201036397/ |access-date=December 22, 2022 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}} He started all 34 games for the Hokies, scoring double-digit points in 31 of those, with his highest single-game point total being 25 against [[2022–23 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]]. Averaging 15.0 points per game, Pedulla was the Hokies' number two scorer that season.{{cite news |last1=Lyttle |first1=Steve |title=Hokies’ Sean Pedulla, one of nine siblings, learned early to battle for what he wanted |url=https://www.pilotonline.com/2023/11/05/hokies-sean-pedulla-one-of-nine-siblings-learned-early-to-battle-for-what-he-wanted/ |access-date=March 7, 2025 |work=The Virginian-Pilot |date=November 5, 2023}} He improved upon this in his junior season. On January 15, 2024, Pedulla was named the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] Player of the Week after putting up 32 points in a win against [[2023–24 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]], following it up with a 33-point performance against [[2023–24 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami]], a new career high.{{cite news |title=VT's Pedulla, ND's Shrewsberry Earn ACC Men’s Basketball Weekly Honors |url=https://theacc.com/news/2024/1/15/vts-pedulla-nds-shrewsberry-earn-acc-mens-basketball-weekly-honors.aspx |access-date=March 7, 2025 |work=Atlantic Coast Conference |date=January 15, 2024}} At the end of the season, Pedulla earned third-team All-ACC honors,{{cite news |title=UNC’s RJ Davis Leads ACC Men’s Basketball 2023-24 Season Honors |url=https://theacc.com/news/2024/3/11/uncs-rj-davis-leads-acc-mens-basketball-2023-24-season-honors.aspx |access-date=March 7, 2025 |work=Atlantic Coast Conference |date=March 11, 2024}} finishing with an average of 16.4 points per game.{{cite news |last1=Tipton |first1=Joe |title=Virginia Tech transfer guard Sean Pedulla commits to Ole Miss |url=https://www.on3.com/college/ole-miss-rebels/news/virginia-tech-transfer-guard-sean-pedulla-commits-to-ole-miss/ |access-date=March 7, 2025 |work=On3 |date=April 24, 2024}} ===Ole Miss=== On March 24, 2024, Pedulla entered the [[NCAA transfer portal|transfer portal]].{{cite news |last1=Romano |first1=Anthony |title=Virginia Tech's Sean Pedulla enters transfer portal |url=https://www.wdbj7.com/2024/03/27/virginia-techs-sean-pedulla-enters-transfer-portal/ |access-date=March 7, 2025 |work=WDBJ |date=March 27, 2024}} A month later, on April 24, Pedulla announced that he was transferring to [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]] over [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]] and [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]]. Pedulla was solid early for the Rebels, scoring 18 points in a half in the December 21 game against [[2024–25 Queens Royals men's basketball team|Queens]].{{cite news |last1=Redding |first1=Jared |title=Rebels pull away in second half, knock off Queens 80-62 behind Sean Pedulla's 25 points |url=https://247sports.com/college/ole-miss/article/ole-miss-queens-mens-basketball-2024-recap-notes-stats-242631228/ |access-date=March 7, 2025 |work=Inside the Rebels |publisher=247Sports |date=December 21, 2024}} On February 27, 2025, Pedulla was named a finalist for the [[Howell Trophy]], awarded to the best college basketball player in the state of Mississippi.{{cite news |title=Sean Pedulla Named Finalist for 2025 Howell Trophy |url=https://olemisssports.com/news/2025/2/27/mens-basketball-sean-pedulla-named-finalist-for-2025-howell-trophy |access-date=March 7, 2025 |work=Ole Miss Sports |publisher=University of Mississippi |date=February 27, 2025}} Two days later, Pedulla hit a game-winning three-pointer against his home state team [[2024–25 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team|Oklahoma]], capping off a 26-point day to solidify Ole Miss' bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2025 NCAA tournament]].{{cite news |last1=Hutchens |first1=Sam |title=Why Sean Pedulla's winning 3-pointer for Ole Miss basketball vs Oklahoma had deeper meaning |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/ole-miss/2025/03/01/ole-miss-basketball-sean-pedulla-game-winner-vs-oklahoma/79466225007/ |access-date=March 7, 2025 |work=Clarion Ledger |date=March 1, 2025}} On March 10, Pedulla was named a third-team All-SEC selection.{{cite news |title=2025 SEC Men's Basketball Awards announced |url=https://www.secsports.com/news/2025/03/2025-sec-mens-basketball-awards-announced |access-date=March 11, 2025 |work=SEC Sports |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=March 10, 2025}} During Ole Miss' opening game in the [[2025 SEC men's basketball tournament|2025 SEC tournament]], Pedulla hit the game-winning three-pointer to secure an 83-80 win over [[2024–25 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]], allowing the Rebels to advance to the quarterfinals.{{cite news |last1=Roberts |first1=Adam |title=Arkansas loses to Ole Miss in back-and-forth battle |url=https://www.4029tv.com/article/arkansas-ole-miss/64177761 |access-date=March 13, 2025 |work=KHBS |date=March 13, 2025}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2025 NBA draft]], Pedulla joined the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for the [[2025 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Announce NBA 2K26 Summer League 2025 Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-announce-nba-2k26-summer-league-2025-roster|website=NBA.com|date=July 4, 2025|access-date=July 12, 2025}} For the [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–26 season]], he was added to the roster of the Blazers' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Rip City Remix]]. On February 20, 2026, Pedulla signed on a two-way contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{Cite web|title=The LA Clippers Sign Guard Sean Pedulla To A Two-Way Contract|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/the-la-clippers-sign-guard-sean-pedulla-to-a-two-way-contract|access-date=April 11, 2026|website=gleague.nba.com|language=en}} He made his NBA debut on March 11 against the [[2025–26 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]], in which he had six points, three assists and one rebound in six minutes. On April 2, Pedulla was named the NBA G League Rookie Of The Year, having averaged 23.6 points, 6.7 assists, 5.0 rebounds, and 1.6 steals across 28 total appearances.{{cite web |title=Sean Pedulla Named 2025-26 Kia NBA G League Rookie Of The Year |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/sean-pedulla-named-2025-26-kia-nba-g-league-rookie-of-the-year |website=NBA.com |access-date=April 8, 2026 |date=April 2, 2026}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2025}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2025–26 Los Angeles Clippers season|L.A.
